Luxor: West Texas Power Prices Drove Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Down 9.13% Bitcoin mining difficulty fell 9.13% on November 14, its largest decline since June. According to Luxor’s Hashrate Index, the drop was driven primarily by surging electricity prices in West Texas rather than falling BTC prices. A sharp decline in wind generation and transmission constraints pushed daily average power prices to $64–$122/MWh from November 7 to 11, above the roughly $54/MWh average breakeven level for miners operating at 25 J/TH. During the October 29–November 14 difficulty period, electricity prices exceeded that breakeven level for 45% of hours, up from 9% in the previous period. Luxor’s analysis attributed 30 percentage points of the 36-point increase to higher electricity prices alone. Based on Texas’s estimated 17% share of global hashrate and the increase in uneconomic mining hours, Luxor calculated that additional curtailment could explain roughly 65 EH/s, or 71%, of the 91 EH/s decline in the network’s 14-day average hashrate. As West Texas power prices eased to $26–$43/MWh from November 13 to 15, estimated network hashrate rebounded to nearly 1,100 EH/s despite a 13% drop in BTC prices between November 11 and 16. With blocks averaging 9.1 minutes since the adjustment, Luxor projected that mining difficulty could rise roughly 10% in the next adjustment if the pace persists, though the estimate remains preliminary. — link

AI Investment Concerns Trigger Market Selloff as Nasdaq 100 Posts Worst Week Since 2020 According to Bloomberg, U.S. stocks tumbled on November 20 as concerns over the sustainability of AI investment, slowing data center expansion and tech earnings prospects intensified. The S&P 500 fell 3.7%, marking its seventh consecutive daily decline and entering correction territory. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 5.6%, posting its worst weekly performance since March 2020. Nvidia plunged 14%, while a semiconductor stock index fell 11%. The selloff spread to cryptocurrencies, precious metals and emerging markets. Bitcoin declined 5.1% to approximately $58,333, Ether fell 8% to $1,601, and spot gold dropped 2.8%. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield declined 11 basis points to 4.93%. Analysts said the market downturn reflected investors reassessing the pace of AI infrastructure development, financing prospects for related projects and expectations for tech earnings growth. — link

Sonic Audit Reveals S Token Supply Is 48% Higher Than Initially Announced Sonic disclosed that its total S token supply stands at 4.70 billion, approximately 48% above the initially announced 3.175 billion. An independent audit found that when 2.12 billion native FTM tokens were minted on Fantom Opera in 2019, approximately 1.47 billion corresponding ERC-20 FTM tokens remained unlocked instead of being locked or burned, becoming a major source of the increased S supply. Sonic said the historical discrepancy remains under investigation. It plans to remove manual minting functionality and burn 91.7 million unallocated S tokens on December 15. — link
